prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` skips pre-parsing whenever *every* member of a union is in a fixed simple-type set {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} — including unions that don't contain `str` at all, e.g. `int | None`. That disables the pre-parse step for plain Optional[int]/Optional[float]/Optional[bool] parameters, regressing the case where a client sends a JSON-encoded numeric string that needs coercion to int/float/bool. #3056 scopes the fix narrowly to the actual failure mode — annotations that reduce to `str | None` — via `_is_optional_str`, and additionally unwraps `Annotated[...]` (`_unwrap_annotated`) so a common pattern like `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` is also covered, which #2032's frozenset membership check does not handle (an `Annotated[str, ...]` member is never equal to the bare `str` type, so it isn't in `_SIMPLE_TYPES` and #2032 would still incorrectly pre-parse it).

PR #2478 solves the same case at the base-class level: its new `_restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error)` dispatcher explicitly special-cases `UrlElicitationRequiredError` by calling `exc_type.from_error(error)` (the identical reconstruction path 2555 hand-rolls), and falls back to `exc_type.from_error_data(error)` for every other MCPError subclass generically. clusters.pick_reason: Same fix target as #3063 but a strict superset: #3063 keys/guards on `str(message.id)`, which (a) collapses JSON-RPC int id `1` and string id "1" into the same key — causing a false 409 or, worse, cross-wiring between an int and string id that JSON-RPC treats as distinct — and (b) doesn't protect the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel from collision with a string id literally equal to "_GET_stream". #3221 introduces a dedicated `_request_stream_key()` that preserves the int/str type distinction (`i:`/`s:` prefixes) and can't collide with `GET_STREAM_KEY`, so it handles every case #3063 handles plus these two edge cases.
